messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: Solaris AI inference goals + next steps

Thanks again for your time this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment moving into the technical deep-dive.

Key pain points you described
- High P95 latency on customer-facing queries (~1.1s observed for short prompts during peak); spikes up to ~2s during concurrent batch runs.
- Variable throughput; platform currently saturates at ~120 QPS for the 70B model and falls back to CPU for bursts.
- Cost unpredictability from elastic scaling and KV cache cold-starts (large prompt prefixes).

Business goals & success criteria (as we captured)
- Reduction of user-facing P95 to 150ms or better for single-turn short prompts (under 64 tokens) for the main chat product.
- Consistent 200–300 QPS sustained for peak traffic windows with graceful degradation to a lower-cost model for overflow.
- Predictable unit economics: target average cost/token reduction of >=30% vs current baseline.

Model & workload notes
- Primary model: open-weights ~70B decoder model (using 4-bit quantized weights in production).
- Typical request length: median 28 tokens input, 40 tokens generation.
- Mix: 85% single-turn chat, 15% multi-turn recommendations with KV cache reuse.

Initial topology options we discussed
- Dedicated GPU pool (A100/NVIDIA H100 equivalent) with pinned model shards + warm KV cache, autoscale for background jobs.
- Hosted fallback to a smaller quantized variant (35B) for overflow.
- VPC-enabled Private control plane for logging/audit (if procurement requires).

Requested next steps (ownership)
1) Solaris: share a 24h representative traffic sample + a short prompt set for eval (Jordan / Elena) — due: Wed 3/3.
2) Redwood: produce a short topology sketch, cost estimate, and a 60-min deep-dive agenda (Neha) — due: Tue 3/2.
3) Schedule technical deep-dive with Solaris infra + model owners (target week of 3/8) — action: Jordan to propose times.

Attachments I'm sending after this thread: a one-page proposal, a sample topology sketch, and a template for traffic samples.

If any of this is off, please flag — otherwise I’ll pack the topology sketch + cost ranges and we can lock a deep-dive.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Neha — thanks, this is helpful and accurate. A few quick clarifications before we lock the deep-dive: 

1) Latency targets: when you say P95 150ms for short prompts, can you confirm whether that assumes a single-request per-GPU serving path (no batching) or with micro-batching (N<=8)? Our ideal user experience requires sub-200ms in single-turn flows.

2) Throughput: our product team expects sustained 250 QPS during weekday peaks; ephemeral batch jobs (indexing / embeddings) may add ~50QPS in off-peak windows.

3) Security: procurement flagged Private/VPC option and SOC2 logs. We’ll need a summary of what telemetry and logs Redwood would keep and how long by default (30/90/365 day options).

Can you attach the topology sketch and a rough cost/rate card so I can route to finance? Also, I can share a 24h traffic sample (sanitized) — I’ll send that by Wed.

I’m copying Elena (infra lead) — she’ll be on the deep-dive. Proposed time windows for the week of 3/8: Tue 10–11am PT, Thu 1–2pm PT.

—Jordan

Jordan — attaching the short topology sketch and the one-page proposal (stubs attached here). A few clarifying notes inline and a proposed 60-minute deep-dive agenda below.

Quick answers to your clarifications:
- The 150ms P95 target assumes a single-request optimized fast path (no large batching) with KV cache warm; micro-batching (N<=4) can still meet sub-200ms if we pre-warm caches and keep sequence lengths short. For long multi-turn calls we expect higher medians and recommend autoscaling policies.
- For sustained 250 QPS we recommend a small fleet of 4–6 high-memory inference nodes (model-specific sizing depends on quantization/sharding) with an autoscaler that provides 20% headroom.
- Telemetry: by default Redwood stores request metadata & tracing (no PII unless you send it) for 90 days; SOC2/compliance packages and extended retention (365d) are available as an add-on. We’ll provide an exportable audit log and KMS integration details in the deep-dive.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood-proposal-v1.pdf — high-level topology options + ballpark cost ranges.
- topology-sketch.png — proposed dedicated pool + hosted fallback + VPC connector.
- solaris-latency-sample-metrics.xlsx — template for traffic sample & example histogram.

Proposed 60-min deep-dive agenda (goal: topology & test plan)
0–10m: introductions + current infra constraints (Solaris)
10–30m: Redwood topology recommendations (dedicated pool sizing, KV cache plans, fallbacks)
30–45m: Performance test plan & telemetry needed (traffic sample format, latency/throughput gates)
45–60m: Action items & timeline (pilot, runbook, procurement checkpoints)

When you confirm a slot I’ll send a calendar invite and a pre-call checklist for Elena’s team (access to a sanitized traffic sample, a few example prompts, and any model-weight constraints).

Next steps (summary):
- Jordan/Elena: share sanitized traffic sample by Wed 3/3.
- Jordan: confirm deep-dive slot (Tue 3/8 10am PT preferred).
- Redwood (Neha/Karthik): finalize topology sketch and begin sizing work after we receive samples.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the calendar invite once you confirm.

Neha Kapoor
